title: Choose the visual world for HC Tracking
question: Your red/gray palette, Somar Sans and the sidebar stay on every option. The roll assigned the Departures Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Departures Board
options.lineage: Split-flap station timetables, adapted to program delivery
options.thesis: Every commitment is a departure: scheduled, actual, and a status everyone can read from across the room.
options.viewport: Dashboard opens on a live board of what is due, late and landed this month (milestones, tasks, transfers, reports), with portfolio figures in flap cells above it.
options.risk: Tips into station kitsch if the flap motif spreads beyond key figures and status rows.

raised.raise: Keyboard-first: a Ctrl+K command line jumps to any record, and system states print as plain status lines, not chrome.
One control propagates: clicking a segment of a page's status strip filters every figure, chart and row on that page.
Capacity is shown as capacity: disbursed fills a committed budget, milestone weights fill 100%, and overflow is marked.
Total colour discipline: status colour owns whole cells flat, with no tinted gradients, glows or decorative shadows.
Density encodes value: matrix and heatmap cells darken by count, so coverage reads before any number is read.

options.label: The Logframe Dossier
options.lineage: Donor proposal packs: logframe matrix, Gantt workplan, budget annex
options.thesis: The app as the living version of the proposal pack your team already writes for every donor.
options.viewport: Dashboard as a cover sheet: the results chain as a matrix with indicators and targets in columns, and the workplan Gantt beneath.
options.risk: The most familiar direction for this audience: it can feel like more paperwork rather than a command system.

options.label: Phosphor Terminal
options.thesis: The portfolio as a scrolling transcript you type into.
options.viewport: A transcript of recent events with a typed prompt.
options.case: Fuses poorly: managers and officers don't identify with a terminal, and donor money reads as log noise.
options.kept: Keyboard-first operation and states that print themselves.
options.risk: Unreadable for non-technical staff; conflicts with the brand palette.

options.label: Miura-fold Sheet
options.thesis: Records unfold from packet to full sheet.
options.viewport: A folded portfolio packet that deploys into the full program sheet.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the fold metaphor obscures status and money.
options.kept: One control propagating across the whole sheet.
options.risk: Heavy geometry for a daily tool.

options.label: Mixtape J-card
options.thesis: Each program as a timed tracklist.
options.viewport: Projects listed as tracks with running times.
options.case: Fuses poorly: playful handwriting undermines donor-facing seriousness.
options.kept: A hard capacity constraint that must not overflow.

options.label: Guide-map Lobes
options.thesis: Programs as swelling lobes of flat colour.
options.viewport: The portfolio drawn as a map of program regions.
options.case: Fuses poorly: its palette overrides the brand, and geography is a false metaphor for programs.

options.label: ASCII Live Scene
options.viewport: Portfolio health as a glyph field.
options.case: Fuses poorly: illegible for exact figures and Arabic text.
options.kept: Density as a direct encoding of value.

options.label: Cloud Quarry
options.thesis: Cutting blocks of weather into buildings.
options.case: Fuses poorly: no identification, no clarity gain.
options.kept: Stacked sections with deliberate gaps: a dense band earns a quiet one.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A best-in-class SaaS operations dashboard, in your brand colours.
canonCard.viewport: KPI card row, two charts, then a recent-activity table.
canonCard.risk: Polished, but indistinguishable from every other admin dashboard, which you asked to avoid.
